display.title: The Four Chochmos, Part 1
display.summary_short: Rabbi Yehuda, who loves hachnasas orchim, saves for a whole year and sets off for the great Leipzig fair with just four gold coins and complete trust in Hashem.
display.summary_long: The storyteller opens in the month of Kislev, listing its many Chassidic Yomim Tovim, from Rosh Chodesh Kislev to the Alter Rebbe's second release on Chanukah. He explains that the Rebbe pours out brachos and we only need to 'catch' them with a good resolution, and tells how the Rebbe Rashab told a fine yeshiva bochur, 'I know who you are better than you know who you are.' Emunas tzaddikim means following the Rebbe's advice, such as learning Chitas, even when we do not understand it. The story begins: Rabbi Yehuda keeps a guest room fit for a king. Hearing of the yearly market in Leipzig, he saves a coin or two each day after giving tzedakah. After a year he has four hundred small coins, which he changes into four gold coins. His wife and his friend Reb Yankel, who gives him a ride, wonder what he can buy with so little, but Rabbi Yehuda trusts that Hashem is in charge of success. At the market nothing suits him until he finds an empty shop where a man named Avram sells 'chochmos', good advice, for one gold coin each. To be continued.
display.lesson: Trust that Hashem is in charge of our success, and follow the advice of a tzaddik even when we do not understand it.
